attempts.label: DANDI:001518
attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging measured with FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paragraph is below, ready to save. Most of the paper's main findings did not hold in this data or could not be tested. The Gd3+ effects, calcium responses, two-pulse recovery and 0.3-us pulses could not be tested because the dandiset lacks those experiments. The dye response ceilings (FluoVolt peaked at 36% against 71%), the dye calibration, the pole dimming and the cosine behaviour near the equator did not reproduce. These tests assume a volts to V/cm conversion that the files and paper do not give, though the ceilings fail at every conversion tried. Only the within-set decline of Di-8-ANEPPS response reproduced, mostly as a drift present at every field strength.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001518, which holds ten escalations of 1-us pulses from 25 to 250 V, five with each dye, imaged by pulsed laser microscopy. It tests the calibration of the two dyes, the FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS responses up to electroporating fields, and Eq. (2) of the paper. The files give the pulse in volts; the factor to V/cm is assumed from the electrode geometry (1400 V/cm at 250 V) and every criterion is also run over a range of factors. The alternating, 0.3-us, Gd3+, Ca2+ and two-pulse experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001518

outcomes.notes: Under the adopted reading (top mapping, background subtracted, equal-area radius, all responding cells, the four sets from 140 to 336 V/cm) FluoVolt gives 6.10% dF per 100 mV (26 +- 2.6) with r 0.775 (Pearson) and 0.743 (uncentred), against 0.96 +- 0.096, and Di-8-ANEPPS 2.37% (9.1 +- 0.91) with r 0.481 and 0.402 (0.78 +- 0.078). Over the 16 top-mapping readings the slopes are 2.72 to 6.10 and 0.83 to 2.37; by experiment 5.36 to 6.64 and 2.20 to 2.53. The slope falls as the factor rises, but not as one over the factor, because the sets at or below 360 V/cm change with it. On a grid from 1.40 to 2.30 V/cm per V in steps of 0.02 the FluoVolt slope is within tolerance at 1.40 to 1.76 and the Di-8-ANEPPS slope at 1.82 to 2.16, with r within tolerance for both dyes throughout (0.90 to 0.92 and 0.79 to 0.84); no factor on that grid or in the sweep from 1.5 to 8 meets the criterion for both dyes, so the result is not reproduced at the factors run. The factors matching each slope, about 1.4 to 2.2, are near the 1.5 to 1.6 implied by the low-field response and below the 4.64 to 7.19 of the electrode geometry. Under the bottom variant, which was set from this same response, the slopes are 23.98 and 10.52 with r 0.908 and 0.824. None of 32 readings meets the criterion for both dyes. With the edge trace the slopes are 4.5 and 1.8 at the adopted factor.
deviations: The pulse is given in volts; the factor to V/cm is assumed to be 5.6 V/cm per V (1400 V/cm at 250 V, the top mapping). A two-dimensional model of the electrodes of Methods 2.2 (rods 0.5 mm in diameter, 1.6 mm apart) gives 4.64 to 7.19 V/cm per V at the midpoint, depending on whether 1.6 mm is the gap or the centre distance. The bottom mapping (43 V/cm at 25 V, 1.72 V/cm per V) matches the paper's dye sensitivities, which fig3-dye-sensitivity tests, and is run as a variant. Every criterion is also run over factors from 1.5 to 8 V/cm per V.
Each field of view holds 3 to 6 cells; the paper used one cell per experiment and does not say which. Experiment means (adopted), the cell nearest the image centre and all cells are run.

The membrane trace is found automatically (peak of the baseline image along rays from the cell centre, 6 samples 1 pixel apart), not drawn by hand; 360 points at equal angles stand for the resampling along the perimeter (Methods 2.3). In some cells the trace is drawn inwards by bright spots inside the cell, and one object in c7 is two touching cells; a trace that follows the cell edge is run as a variant over every criterion and changes no result at the adopted factor.

Pixel size 0.267 um (16-um camera pixels over the 60x objective of Methods 2.3) is assumed; the files give none. The mean radius is 6.7 um with the peak trace and 9.9 um with the edge trace, against the about 8 um the paper uses in Eq. (2).
Frame 0 and other dark frames (laser misfires) are left out, so most baselines have 39 images.

Background subtraction (median of cell-free pixels of the same image) is adopted; the paper states it only for Ca2+ imaging (Methods 2.4). No subtraction and the camera offset alone are run as variants.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping the FluoVolt smooth does not depart from the line at |IMPC| of 220 mV and above under any LOWESS span (0 of 48 grid points; 12 of 42 with 50-mV bins); it lies above the line (107 to 113% of it at +220 mV, 128 to 134% at -220 mV). Di-8-ANEPPS departs at 22 to 23 grid points under every smooth, near zero on the positive side, from the uniform bleaching offset. With each profile's offset removed FluoVolt still does not depart, and Di-8-ANEPPS departs under span 0.3 and bins but not under 0.5 and 0.75. Under the bottom variant FluoVolt departs from 220 mV under every smooth, but Di-8-ANEPPS departs at 58 to 64 points (40 to 50 with the offset removed). No factor from 1.5 to 8 meets the criterion.
deviations: Points, line and readings as in fig3-dye-sensitivity (adopted reading); LOWESS with delta of 1% of the IMPC range, a standard speed-up.
The fit through the origin keeps the uniform bleaching offset of each profile, as the paper reports bleaching in its own Di-8-ANEPPS dF (Results 3.2, paragraph 3); removing it is run as a variant.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping the per-image cathodic dF at 360 V/cm is 23.5% (experiment means; 20.1 for the cell nearest the centre, 24.1 over all cells) against 66 +- 6.6, and the anodic value at 570 V/cm -35.8% (-33.7, -38.6) against -83 +- 8.3. The cathodic maximum is 35.9% at 570 V/cm. Over all 19 sets the largest experiment-mean cathodic value is 36.1% and the most negative anodic -49.5%; per experiment 43.6% and -61.1%. With the camera offset as background 17.3% and -25.2%, without background 12.1% and -17.9%. The trace check (rings within 3 pixels of the trace, and the edge trace) does not bring the means near the paper's values. The magnitudes fail under every factor from 1.5 to 8.
deviations: The mean of per-image dF over the pulse images equals the collapsed-image dF, as both use the same F0; the Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 measures coincide.
FluoVolt n is 5 experiments here, against 4 in the paper.
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: In the baseline images (top mapping, experiment means, sets at the paper's levels, 10-image windows) the cathodic pole changes by -3.34% at 780 V/cm (2-tailed paired t-test p = 0.018, n = 5) and -2.82% at 1000 V/cm (p = 0.003); the other 14 changes lie between -3.04% and +0.64%. Across readings 1 to 4 of 16 baseline tests at the levels and 4 to 9 of 38 over all sets are significant; with experiment means over all sets 4 of 38 (about 1.9 expected by chance), and 32 of 38 changes are negative, a small bleaching drift. In the pulse images at 1000 to 1400 V/cm none of 6 tests differs with experiment means (changes -0.78 to -2.01%, p 0.09 to 0.54), 0 or 1 under other readings. The criterion counts any significant baseline change. In the factor sweep it is met only at 3.5 V/cm per V (at 8 with the edge trace).
deviations: The sets are those nearest the paper's levels; all 19 sets are shown as a variant.
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping the largest mean cathodic dF over levels is 35.9% (570 V/cm; 34.4 and 35.7 under the other cell readings) against 71 +- 10, and the most negative anodic value -49.5% (1200 V/cm; -49.9, -51.1) against -83.5 +- 5; under the bottom variant 31.7 to 35.8% and -48.8 to -51.1%. There is no 43 V/cm set under the top mapping; at 150 V/cm measured IMP is already below IMPC (ratios 0.10 and 0.20, paired p < 0.001 and 0.001), so the match fails there. Measured IMP is below IMPC at every level from 230 V/cm (ratios 0.06 to 0.25). No factor from 1.5 to 8 meets the maxima.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: The cathodic dF at 360 V/cm is 23.5% under the top mapping (20.1 and 24.1 under the other cell readings; 25.5 to 27.7% under the bottom variant) against 71 +- 10. At 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm it is 28.9, 25.5 and 21.2% (experiment means; the second measured value is their mean), outside 40.5 to 55%. The largest mean cathodic dF of any set is 36.1%, below the 61% bound, so no factor meets it.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping, with experiment means, both poles rise at every step from 150 to 570 V/cm (cathodic -1.6, 2.7, 6.6, 13.0%; anodic -6.2, -7.7, -10.6, -16.7%), as they do over all cells and without background subtraction. With the cell nearest the centre the anodic pole falls from 150 to 230 V/cm (-5.7 to -4.5%). The step from 43 V/cm cannot be tested, as that level has no set. In the factor sweep the criterion holds at every factor from 2 to 8; below 2 there is no 570 V/cm set.
deviations: Under the top mapping the 43 V/cm level has no set, so the steps are tested from 150 V/cm.
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping the cathodic |dF| at the end of the pulse images is below the start in every set from 780 V/cm under every cell reading and both windows (experiment means, 10-image windows, 19.8 to 17.1, 22.2 to 19.7, 24.4 to 20.8 and 27.0 to 22.4%; p 0.034, 0.069, 0.037, 0.142). The anodic pole declines in none of these sets with experiment means and 10-image windows, so reading (d) fails; reading (c) is adopted. Drift control: below 780 V/cm the cathodic |dF| also falls within the set in 9 of 11 sets (mean -1.76%); from 780 V/cm by -3.32% on average, of which -2.15% is an offset shared by both poles and -1.17% the polarization amplitude. Most of the decline is a drift present at every field strength. The criterion holds at every factor from 5.6 to 8 in the sweep; below 5.6 there is no 1400 V/cm set.
deviations: The text does not name the pole; reading (c), the cathodic pole, is assumed, as the paper places the damage at the cathodic pole (Results 3.1, the cathodic pole dims at 780 V/cm; Results 3.4, the reduction is more pronounced at the cathodic pole). Reading (d) is shown.
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping Di-8-ANEPPS pole dF is largest at 1400 V/cm (24.3% and -29.2%, experiment means), not at 570 V/cm (13.0% and -16.7%), against 57 +- 14 and -55 +- 4. Measured IMP is below IMPC at every level, including 150 to 360 V/cm (ratios -0.14 to 0.54), so the second condition fails too. The largest Di-8-ANEPPS means of any set are 24.3% and -29.2%, so no factor meets the magnitudes; with the edge trace they are 25.1% and -30.4%.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Over the first 10 pulse images the largest mean cathodic dF is 27.0% (top mapping, 1400 V/cm, experiment means; 21.0 for the cell nearest the centre) against 66 +- 15. It is above the 60-image maximum (24.3%) under every reading. The largest first-10 value of any set is 27.0%, so no factor meets the criterion.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping both poles keep growing from 780 to 1400 V/cm (cathodic 18.1, 20.4, 22.5, 24.3%; anodic -21.2, -25.7, -27.8, -29.2%, experiment means), so condition (1) fails under every cell reading. The cathodic value at 1400 V/cm differs from zero (p < 0.001; 0.053 for the cell nearest the centre), and the anodic -29.2% is within -30 +- 3. No factor from 5 to 8 meets the criterion; below 5 there is no 1400 V/cm set.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping measured IMP in the arcs beside the equator is below IMPC at 570, 780 and 1000 V/cm in most arcs (ratios -0.15 to 0.82 over readings); of 12 arc-level tests per reading, 9 to 11 differ with 15-degree arcs and all 12 with 30-degree arcs. The arcs on the cathode side of 90 degrees read about zero or negative (ratios -0.13, 0.10, 0.04 with experiment means and 15-degree arcs) where IMPC is positive. No factor in the sweep meets the criterion.
deviations: Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping the mean cathodic dF at 780 V/cm (18.1%) is above that at 570 V/cm (13.0%), so condition (1) fails under every cell and background reading (10.6 against 12.1% for the cell nearest the centre; 7.4 against 9.9% without background). At 1400 V/cm the peak of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies 12 to 46 degrees from the pole, so condition (2) holds. No factor from 5 to 8 meets the criterion; below 5 there is no 1400 V/cm set.
deviations: Figure 1's cell is not identified; the Di-8-ANEPPS escalation cells are used, as the criterion says.
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Under the top mapping, normalized to the 150 V/cm set (25 V), no reading meets the criterion. At 25 V both poles share a bleaching offset (mean of the poles -3.9% in Di-8-ANEPPS), which makes the anodic |dF| at 150 V/cm too large and the cathodic one too small. The anodic pole with experiment means and per-cell normalization (the measured values) gives 1.46 at 560 V/cm (1.5 +- 0.15) and 1.62 at 760 V/cm (2 +- 0.2), and 1.72, 1.76 and 2.08 at 1000 to 1400 V/cm, so it exceeds 2 only at 1400; every datapoint of that reading is below the line at p < 0.01. Its values are nearest the paper's, but it is the reading the offset affects most. The cathodic ratios are 0.63 to 0.94. The mean of the poles, in which the offset cancels, gives 0.55 to 0.85 with experiment means, so the measured polarization lies above the linear line. With per-cell normalization over all cells the mean of the poles gives ratios such as -10.7 and 16.9, because the 150 V/cm values are near zero; those ratios carry no information. Only factors 5.6 and 6.25 have every level, and neither meets the criterion.
deviations: The 560 and 760 V/cm of Results 3.7 are the 570 and 780 V/cm sets (claims file header).
Factor, cell, trace, pixel and background choices as in fig3-dye-sensitivity.

outcomes.notes: Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives f = 1.498 for the intact membrane. A 10-fold rise reduces IMP by 1.33% under reading (a) and 1.20% under (b), against 2 +- 0.2; a 15.2-fold rise is needed for 2%. A 100-fold rise gives 11.87% and 11.75%, within 12 +- 1.2. The qualitative point holds, with 3.9% at 30-fold.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds ten escalations of 1-us pulses, 19 sets each from 25 to 250 V, five with FluoVolt and five with Di-8-ANEPPS, all from 2025-01-24. It holds none of the alternating sets (Fig. 2C, D), 0.3-us pulses (Fig. 4D), Gd3+ experiments (Fig. 5), Ca2+ imaging (Fig. 6) or two-pulse experiments (Fig. 7). Its voltages span a factor of 10, so it cannot hold the paper's 43 to 1400 V/cm escalation (a factor of 33, in 9 sets). The paper's FluoVolt series has n = 4; the dandiset has 5.

The files give the pulse amplitude in volts, and the paper reports field strengths in V/cm from Sim4Life modelling; neither the files, the paper nor its reference [20] give the factor between them, so the sets cannot be matched to the paper's field strengths without assuming one.

Every file states an electrode distance of 1.00 mm, while the paper's Methods 2.2 state 1.6 mm. A two-dimensional model of two 0.5-mm rods gives 8.0 to 17.5 V/cm per volt at the midpoint for 1.00 mm and 4.6 to 7.2 for 1.6 mm (gap or centre distance). The paper's dye calibration, applied to the low-field response, would imply about 1.5 V/cm per volt, so either the stated geometry and voltage do not describe the field, or the dyes respond less here than in the paper.
Each field of view holds 3 to 6 cells, while the paper analysed one cell per experiment. Nothing in the files identifies the cell analysed, or gives cell outlines.

The files give no pixel size, no field direction and no description of which images carry the pulse. The field direction (cathode-facing side towards the bottom of the image, 94 to 106 degrees) and the pulse onset at image 41 are clear from the data.
Frame 0 is dark (laser not fired) in 175 of 190 sets, and 51 other frames in 45 sets are dark; the files do not mention it. With these frames left out, most baselines have 39 lit images, not 40.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) What field strength in V/cm does each pulse amplitude in the files correspond to, and are these the escalations of Fig. 2A, 2B and 3 or other experiments? The attempt assumed 1400 V/cm at 250 V (5.6 V/cm per volt), from the electrode geometry, and ran 1.5 to 8. (2) Which cell in each field of view was analysed? The attempt ran experiment means, the cell nearest the image centre and all cells. (3) Was background subtracted from the laser images, as for Ca2+ (Methods 2.4)? The attempt subtracted the cell-free median; without it dF halves. (4) What is the pixel size? The attempt assumed 0.267 um.

Eq. (2) with the constants the Methods give (lambda_i 0.4 S/m, lambda_o 1.64 S/m, R 8 um, d 5 nm, lambda_m 3e-7 S/m) gives a 1.3% IMP reduction for a 10-fold rise in membrane conductivity, while Results 3.5 says about 2%; the 100-fold value (11.9%) agrees with the stated 12%.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested helper functions on a synthetic polarized cell and modelled the electrode field. Its report gave its own outcome for each claim; it agreed with 21 of 30. Its other points: the header still carried an outcome table (B10, now updated to the revised outcomes); background reading (b) sits about 120 counts above the camera offset (B7, a camera-offset reading is added: FluoVolt 17.3% and -25.2% at the claim's levels, between readings a and b); the responding-cell selection uses the cells' own response and the experiment reading averages 1 to 5 cells (B8, kept, the three cell readings are all shown); the pole values at all 19 sets are now printed as numbers.

disagreements.reason: Under top, condition 1 fails in all 6 readings: cathodic dF is higher at 780 than at 570 V/cm (e.g. 18.1 vs 13.0%, cell 50). Under bottom there is no 570 V/cm set. Di-8 cathodic dF rises through 90 to 250 V, so condition 1 also fails for any factor that puts 570 and 780 V/cm inside the data. The sets exist; what is missing is the V/cm factor, so the block reason would be metadata_insufficient, and under any physically plausible factor the sets reach 570 to 1400 V/cm (B2).

Under both factors, |dF| rises at every step on experiment and all-cells means. It fails for the centre cell, which is the closest reading to the paper's one cell per experiment. The 570 V/cm level exists only under top, and 43 V/cm exists only under bottom.

Reproduced only if the factor is top-like. Under top the cathodic end is below the start in every set from 780 V/cm, under both start/end readings. The anodic pole does not decline, so reading (d) fails. Most of the cathodic drop is a drift shared by both poles: at 780 V/cm the shared offset drops about 1.9% while the polarization amplitude drops about 0.8%, and no low-field set was run as a control for drift (B6, C).

Blocked as metadata_insufficient. The slope scales directly with the volts-to-V/cm factor. That factor is not recorded, and the adopted value was chosen by matching these same slopes, so the test is circular. Correlation coefficients are within tolerance under bottom (FluoVolt 0.90 to 0.91, Di-8 0.80 to 0.82). Even with the fitted factor, no reading meets both slopes (0 of 32). Under physically plausible factors the slopes would be 3 to 4 times too low. The bottom factor also does not fit the electrode geometry, which gives about 4.6 to 7.2 V/cm per V for 1.6 mm (B1).

The largest Di-8 means over all 19 sets are 24.3% and -29.2%, against 57 +- 14 and -55 +- 4. This holds for every factor that includes 570 V/cm. Measured IMP is also already below IMPC at 43 to 360 V/cm.
The largest first-10 mean is 27.0%, against 66 +- 15, under any factor.
Not reproduced only if the factor is top-like. Under top, cathodic dF rises from 780 to 1400 V/cm (18.1 to 24.3%) and is non-zero at 1400 V/cm (p < 0.001). Only the anodic -29.2% meets its target.

Not reproduced only if the factor is top-like. 9 to 12 of 12 arcs differ in every reading. Some differences do not depend on the factor: the cathode-side arcs near 90 degrees read about zero or negative where IMPC is positive.

Not reproduced only if the factor is top-like. Best reading (anodic pole, experiment means): 1.46 at 560 V/cm passes, 1.62 at 780 V/cm fails against 2 +- 0.2, and 1000 to 1200 V/cm ratios are 1.72 to 1.77, not above 2. In the per-cell normalization for the mean-pole reading the 150 V/cm values are near zero, so the ratios become meaningless (-10.7, 16.9) (B9).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 30 outcomes and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. It checked rod_field_per_volt against the line-charge solution and found the factor of 5.6 V/cm per V reasonable. It found statements the outputs do not support, all corrected: the baseline range in cell 38 and the fig2a-fluovolt-stable notes; the one-over-factor slopes in cell 26 and the fig3-dye-sensitivity notes; the round-1 count in this record (it agreed with 21 of 30, not 19); and the README's 17 minutes, which no output showed (the README now gives the 11 minutes of this run, the notebook comment 10 minutes for the load). It found every round-1 point resolved except the untested interval of factors between 1.72 and 2.0 for fig3-dye-sensitivity, now run on a fine grid, and asked for the bleaching offset to be described in fig7b-charging-during-pulse.
